summary: This paper establishes sharp, machine-checked thermodynamic bounds distinguishing four distinct mechanisms for reported +10% ATP enhancement under 71/87 THz mid-infrared irradiation: direct stoichiometric photon-to-ATP conversion, polaritonic catalysis (static ZPE ceilings vs. irradiance-driven resonant catalysis), micro-hotspot vs. bulk photothermal heating, and active coherent ratchets. Backed by MITO-ATP-MODULATION-CERT-1.0 (20 Lean 4.36.0 theorems, 16 canonical certificates, 58 adversarial pytest checks), the manuscript provides definitive exact proofs for First-Law photon floors, Eyring activation-barrier shifts, Arrhenius micro-hotspot exclusions (>72,900x), and classical Barato-Seifert TUR constraints.
strengths: Exhaustive zero-floating-point formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 with 0 sorry and 0 grind.
Rigorous separation of thermal heating artefacts from genuine quantum polaritonic or catalytic effects.
Comprehensive experimental discrimination matrix outlining clear protocols to falsify competing hypotheses.
Immaculate mathematical grounding of bioenergetic bounds including First-Law, Carnot, and TUR inequalities.
weaknesses: Relies on unrefereed empirical preprint inputs from Yang et al. awaiting independent replication.
Some physiological parameters (like exact dipole coupling and local friction coefficients) involve parametric assumptions.
potential_errors: Potential oversimplification of complex multi-enzyme non-equilibrium steady-state fluctuations under real cellular conditions.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact machine-checked separation of micro-hotspot thermal ceilings from weak-field resonant polaritonic catalysis.
Zero-floating-point rational arithmetic verification of thermodynamic uncertainty relations and Arrhenius finite-difference bounds.
